lines.text: How does this cell fit? Its pipe is narrower than it is.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ dˈʌz ðɪs sˈɛl fˈɪt? ɪts pˈaɪp ɪz nˈaɹəʊə ðɐn ɪt ˈɪz.

lines.text: Each one is a dented disc, pressed in on both sides. It even threw out its own nucleus. And they outnumber all your other cells put together.
lines.phonemes: ˈiːtʃ wˈɒn ɪz ɐ dˈɛntɪd dˈɪsk, pɹˈɛst ɪn ˌɒn bˈəʊθ sˈaɪdz. ɪt ˈiːvən θɹˈuː ˈaʊt ɪts ˈəʊn njˈuːkliəs . and ðeɪ aʊtnˈʌmbəɹ ˈɔːl jɔːɹ ˈʌðə sˈɛlz pˌʊt təɡˈɛðə.

lines.text: Follow one as the pipes split, and split again, into the tiniest ones. There's no room to pass, so they go in single file.
lines.phonemes: fˈɒləʊ wˈɒn az ðə pˈaɪps splˈɪt, and splˈɪt ɐɡˈɛn, ˌɪntʊ ðə tˈaɪniɪst wˌɒnz. ðeəz nˈəʊ ɹˈuːm tə pˈas, sˌəʊ ðeɪ ɡˌəʊ ɪn sˈɪŋɡəl fˈaɪl.

lines.text: You'd guess its skin stretches to fit. It barely does. That dent gives it spare skin, so it folds up neatly like a parachute instead.
lines.phonemes: juːd ɡˈɛs ɪts skˈɪn stɹˈɛtʃɪz tə fˈɪt. ɪt bˈeəli dˈʌz. ðat dˈɛnt ɡˈɪvz ɪt spˈeə skˈɪn, sˌəʊ ɪt fˈəʊldz ˌʌp nˈiːtli lˈaɪk ɐ pˈaɹəʃˌuːt ɪnstˈɛd.

lines.text: The tightest squeeze is less than half its width. And it does this its whole life, over and over, for about four months.
lines.phonemes: ðə tˈaɪtɪst skwˈiːz ɪz lˈɛs ðɐn hˈɑːf ɪts wˈɪtθ. and ɪt dˈʌz ðɪs ɪts hˈəʊl lˈaɪf, ˌəʊvəɹ and ˈəʊvə, fɔːɹ ɐbˌaʊt fˈɔː mˈʌnθs.

lines.text: Sickle cells lose that dent, stiffen, and can jam where oxygen gets dropped off. That dent has a job.
lines.phonemes: sˈɪkəl sˈɛlz lˈuːz ðat dˈɛnt, stˈɪfən, and kan dʒˈam wˌeəɹ ˈɒksɪdʒən ɡˈɛts dɹˈɒpt ˈɒf. ðat dˈɛnt hɐz ɐ dʒˈɒb.

lines.text: Meanwhile, as you watched, your bones made over a hundred million new ones.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːnwaɪl, az juː wˈɒtʃt, jɔː bˈəʊnz mˌeɪd ˌəʊvəɹ ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd mˈɪliən njˈuː wˌɒnz.

lines.text: Next: what this cell carries. Room for about a billion passengers.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: wˌɒt ðɪs sˈɛl kˈaɹiz. ɹˈuːm fɔːɹ ɐbˌaʊt ɐ bˈɪliən pˈasɪndʒəz.
